name: Vulnerability Discovery & Disclosure
description: Finding vulnerabilities at scale, CVE/patch analysis, bug bounties, and disclosure processes.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security papers in this area show vulnerability discovery branching out from classic software bugs toward whole new attack surfaces. Some studied the systems we increasingly depend on, like the power grid in "BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid" (2018) and the smart contracts behind cryptocurrencies in "teEther: Gnawing at Ethereum to Automatically Exploit Smart Contracts" (2018). Just as important, researchers turned the lens on the disclosure process itself, asking whether crowd-sourced reports could even be trusted in "Understanding the Reproducibility of Crowd-reported Security Vulnerabilities" (2018), and whether bug bounties had any rigorous footing in "Enter the Hydra: Towards Principled Bug Bounties and Exploit-Resistant Smart Contracts" (2018).

By 2019 and 2020 the field's center of gravity shifted toward scalable automation, especially fuzzing and patch analysis. Firmware fuzzing matured with "FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation" (2019), and the fuzzing literature grew more sophisticated with smarter scheduling in "EcoFuzz: Adaptive Energy-Saving Greybox Fuzzing as a Variant of the Adversarial Multi-Armed Bandit" (2020) and concurrency-aware bug hunting in "MUZZ: Thread-aware Grey-box Fuzzing for Effective Bug Hunting in Multithreaded Programs" (2020). In parallel, the patch and CVE side professionalized: "Towards the Detection of Inconsistencies in Public Security Vulnerability Reports" (2019) exposed how unreliable CVE/NVD metadata can be, while "MVP: Detecting Vulnerabilities using Patch-Enhanced Vulnerability Signatures" (2020) used patches to find recurring vulnerabilities at scale.

Around the same time the community pushed discovery into harder, more realistic targets. Cyber-physical and automotive systems came under scrutiny in "RVFuzzer: Finding Input Validation Bugs in Robotic Vehicles through Control-Guided Testing" (2019) and "Plug-N-Pwned: Comprehensive Vulnerability Analysis of OBD-II Dongles" (2020), and exploitability, not just bug-finding, became a goal in "KOOBE: Towards Facilitating Exploit Generation of Kernel Out-Of-Bounds Write Vulnerabilities" (2020). Embedded and firmware work then leaned on rehosting and emulation, as in "Jetset: Targeted Firmware Rehosting for Embedded Systems" (2021), with directed fuzzing growing more goal-aware in "Constraint-guided Directed Greybox Fuzzing" (2021).

Most recently the area has widened to the security of machine-learning systems themselves, treating models as a new class of vulnerable software. Hardware-level and microarchitectural flaws stayed prominent in "Half-Double: Hammering From the Next Row Over" (2022), but the newest work targets ML and LLM supply chains directly, from "Hidden Trigger Backdoor Attack on NLP Models via Linguistic Style Manipulation" (2022) to "Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs" (2024). The throughline across all these years is a steady move from finding individual bugs by hand to systematically discovering, exploiting, and triaging weaknesses at scale across ever more diverse systems.

milestones.title: BlackIoT: IoT Botnet of High Wattage Devices Can Disrupt the Power Grid
milestones.note: expanded vulnerability discovery to cyber-physical attack surfaces by showing IoT botnets could destabilize the power grid

milestones.title: Understanding the Reproducibility of Crowd-reported Security Vulnerabilities
milestones.note: questioned the reliability of crowd-sourced vulnerability reports, foregrounding disclosure-quality as a research problem

milestones.title: FIRM-AFL: High-Throughput Greybox Fuzzing of IoT Firmware via Augmented Process Emulation
milestones.note: made high-throughput greybox fuzzing of IoT firmware practical, a key step toward bug-finding at scale

milestones.title: Towards the Detection of Inconsistencies in Public Security Vulnerability Reports
milestones.note: revealed pervasive inconsistencies in CVE/NVD data, spurring work on automated vulnerability-report analysis

milestones.title: MVP: Detecting Vulnerabilities using Patch-Enhanced Vulnerability Signatures
milestones.note: turned security patches into signatures to detect recurring vulnerabilities at scale, tightly linking patch and CVE analysis

milestones.title: KOOBE: Towards Facilitating Exploit Generation of Kernel Out-Of-Bounds Write Vulnerabilities
milestones.note: shifted the goal from finding bugs to assessing exploitability via automated kernel exploit generation

milestones.title: Constraint-guided Directed Greybox Fuzzing
milestones.note: advanced directed fuzzing toward targeted, goal-aware bug reproduction and discovery

milestones.title: Instruction Backdoor Attacks Against Customized LLMs
milestones.note: extended vulnerability discovery to the emerging LLM supply chain, marking the area's pivot to ML-system security
